title: SLO Orchestrator with cost-latency ratchet for safe rollouts
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Implement an SLO Orchestrator service and rollout policy that generates automated rollback recommendations and optional automatic evictions based on a composite SLO signal. The composite signal combines latency (p50/p95), request error rate, token cost per request, and throughput. The distinct innovation is a cost-latency ratchet: when token-cost increases relative to baseline while latency remains stable, the ratchet raises sensitivity to cost regressions; conversely when latency regresses the ratchet prioritizes latency signals. The system should be safe for canary/A-B/staged rollouts and support shadow traffic configs.
design_notes: Composite SLO = weighted sum of normalized signals: w1*latency_p95_norm + w2*error_rate_norm + w3*token_cost_norm + w4*throughput_pressure_norm
Default weights initially set to {latency:0.45, error:0.3, cost:0.15, throughput:0.1}; weights are tunable per-customer and per-release via rollout policy
Ratchet behavior: a hysteresis window + exponential sensitivity multiplier when cost drift exceeds 10% vs baseline over 1h
Signal smoothing: use Bayesian online changepoint detection to avoid reacting to transients during traffic ramps
Action types: advisory (notify + annotate rollout), partial-evacuation (shift 50% of canary traffic back), full-rollback (evacuate new variant), and throttled fallback to cheaper model variant
Safety constraints: minimum canary time 5m, minimum sample size 500 requests for automatic actions, manual approval required for accounts with enterprise-safeguard label
Metrics instrumentation: per-ticket streaming metrics (token_cost, model_latency_ms, status_code_category, request_count) and cohort tagging for region/model-size
Store decisions and scoring trace in rollout audit log for explainability and postmortem
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator exposes an API to register rollout with target SLOs and weights
Simulated canary tests (see test harness) show >90% true-positive detection for injected 20% latency regressions within 10 minutes
Injected token-cost spike (25%) triggers cost-ratchet escalation and results in advisory alert within configured SLO window
Automatic rollback action can be executed end-to-end in lab environments when sample size >= 500 and auto-rollback enabled
Audit log contains human-readable rationale with top-3 contributing signals for every action
Dashboard shows composite score and per-signal decomposition for each rollout and can filter by cohort/region

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives during traffic spikes — Mitigation: require minimum sample size + changepoint detection
Risk: Cost signal noisy due to caching effects — Mitigation: normalize token cost by baseline cached-hit ratio and use 1h rolling baseline
Risk: Over-reacting to error anomalies from downstream infra — Mitigation: correlate with infra metrics and lower auto-rollback weight when downstream fault detected
notes_for_oncall: Rollback actions will write a RolloutDecision event to /events/rollouts. Oncall can annotate and manually override via Console > Rollouts.
If automatic rollback triggers unexpectedly, run 'orchestrator audit <rollout_id>' to retrieve signal decomposition and sample traces.
Escalation path: platform-oncall -> Priya Shah -> Lucas Chen
